answer_1.quote: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been able to fool humans into thinking their outputs are humanwritten for roughly four years.
answer_1.outputs: The paper studies machine-generated text across 8 domains: Books, News, Reddit, Reviews, Wikipedia, Recipes, Poetry, Abstracts, and additional domains in RAID-extra: Python Code, Czech News, German News.

answer_2.quote: On average, models are more repetitive than humans as measured by Self-BLEU and typically generate shorter passages (see Table ). The mean perplexity is lower for models than humans, according to LLaMA 7B and GPT 2 XL.
